title: Railways Adds 400 Special Train Trips as Diwali-Chhath Demand Overwhelms IRCTC
excerpt: Passengers saw 'high load' and 'regret' within minutes of booking windows opening for mid-November journeys; East Central Railway's 16 festival specials run September 16 to November 30.
body:
• IRCTC bookings for Diwali and Chhath Puja journeys are showing "high load" and "regret" errors within minutes of the 8 am opening, with waiting lists crossing 100 and even 200 on Bihar-bound trains.
  • The Railways has approved roughly 400 trips of special trains to Bihar between October 1 and November 30, with East Central Railway finalizing schedules for 16 festival specials in the first phase.
  • Special services will connect more than 10 cities — Delhi, Chandigarh, Firozpur Cantt, Rishikesh and others — with Patna, Patliputra, Muzaffarpur and Jogbani, at weekly, twice-weekly and daily frequencies.
  • Northern Railway has added its own festival specials, including Delhi-Varanasi, Ayodhya-Anand Vihar and Chandigarh-Patna services running through November.

The annual festival travel crunch has arrived early. Passengers trying to book train tickets home to Bihar for Diwali and Chhath Puja found IRCTC's booking portal throwing "high load" and "regret" messages within minutes of the 8 am opening on Sunday, as the 60-day advance reservation window opened for mid-November journeys. When Mint checked the IRCTC app around 8 am, most Bihar-bound sections showed "regret," with waiting lists on some trains already past 100 — and past 200 in some classes.

Social media filled with frustration. One X user wrote to Railway Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw that despite logging in two months in advance, "the app crashes and shows a 'Regret'." Another asked: "If REGRET happens just a few minutes after ticket booking starts, then how will the common passenger get home? During festivals, trains are a necessity for the public, not some VIP facility."

The scale of the rush

Indian Railways allows regular bookings up to 60 days before travel, excluding the date of journey — so tickets for mid-November travel went on sale this week. Even booking at sharp 8 am was no guarantee. "Railway was, is, and will always be a mess," one user posted. "Tried booking a Chhath ticket to Bihar at 8 AM — site stayed busy until 8:12, then started working on and off only after all tickets were already sold out."

https://youtube.com/watch?v=kkOYRBijGwA

""Railway was, is, and will always be a mess," one user posted."

The pressure is concentrated on routes to Bihar, the epicenter of Chhath Puja celebrations, where millions of migrant workers return home each year. Reports show "regret" within 15–30 minutes on key dates for the Delhi-Patna, Delhi-Gorakhpur and Mumbai-Patna corridors.

Special trains announced

In response, the Railways has approved around 400 trips of special trains to Bihar for the Dussehra, Diwali and Chhath period, running between October 1 and November 30. The East Central Railway finalized the first phase — 16 festival specials — on September 9, connecting more than 10 cities with Bihar at weekly, twice-weekly and daily frequencies.

The headline routes, per East Central Railway's schedule:

  • Delhi-Sitamarhi (04009/04010): Thursdays October 15–November 19, return Saturdays October 17–November 21.
  • Anand Vihar-Patliputra (04095): daily from October 1 to November 30 — one of the highest-capacity options for Delhi travelers.
  • Anand Vihar-Laukaha Bazar: daily from September 16 to November 30.
  • Rishikesh-Muzaffarpur (04313/04314): Sundays October 4–November 29, return Mondays October 5–November 30.
  • Chandigarh-Patna (04511/04512): Thursdays October 1–November 27, return Fridays October 2–November 27.
  • Firozpur Cantt-Patna (04615/04616): Tuesdays October 6–November 24, return Wednesdays October 7–November 25.
  • Anand Vihar-Jogbani (04007/04008): Saturdays October 10–November 7, return Sundays October 11–November 8.
  • Anand Vihar-Muzaffarpur (04027/04028): Tuesdays and Fridays October 13–November 24, return Wednesdays and Saturdays October 14–November 25.

Northern Railway has added its own festival specials, including Delhi-Varanasi (04209/04210, October 2–November 28), Ayodhya-Anand Vihar (04213/04214, October 1–November 30) and a Chandigarh-Patna service running October 1–November 27.

Booking strategy

Travel advisories for the season are consistent: log in before 8 am, keep a saved passenger list, and pay via UPI for speed. Passengers can filter for special trains in IRCTC's "Special Trains" option rather than searching only regular services. If general quota sells out, Tatkal opens at 10 am for AC classes and 11 am for non-AC — though agents are barred from the initial window.

Diaspora angle

For NRIs flying into Delhi or Mumbai and connecting onward to Bihar or eastern Uttar Pradesh for the festivals, the message is to book domestic rail legs early — and to check special-train availability rather than only regular trains, which are already waitlisted. International travelers should also note the updated refund rules: full automatic refunds apply when the Railways cancels an e-ticketed service, with sliding deductions of 25% and 50% closer to departure, and no refunds on Tatkal unless the service is cancelled.

What's next

The first phase covers 16 specials; further announcements are expected as the festival dates approach, and crowd-management advisories at major stations will likely intensify through October. With demand already overwhelming the 8 am window, passengers who miss out should track newly announced specials — earlier availability typically opens on new runs before regular trains clear their waitlists.
